properties.details_shown: Fog, tar, and gulls; the far piers are rotting. At pier four in the morning, fog still sits on the docks, with gulls everywhere.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.

changes.why: Adds the description shown at pier four while preserving earlier details.

properties.role: Tide-reader offering to row the party to the old chapel by day.
properties.played_as: Whispers as though the water might hear her; avoids eye contact and watches the tide line. Grey braid, salt-stained coat, mending a net.
properties.wants: Will row the party by day, never at night; offers to be at pier four tomorrow at first light.

sources.quote: There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.
Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
Sela, Sella, the dockhands say it both ways.
She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Records the new voiced NPC, her canonical name and alias, manner, and conditional offer.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.

changes.why: Locates the party's meeting with Sela.

properties.statement: Sela says Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; she reports her grandmother's account that the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Records Sela's historical claim and marks the warm-water account as hearsay.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Connects the attributed flooding account to the existing mine.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. Entrance is a black mouth in chalk with a half-rotted timber frame and an overturned rusted cart. Warm air smells of old candle wax. Thirty paces in, warm black water floods the tunnel; wet hymn-book pages float on it and cling to the walls.
properties.state: Closed; tunnel flooded about thirty paces in with warm black water.

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side. The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: Adds directly observed mine details and its flooded condition.

change.name: A hymn page marked M. Brand in Saltmere

properties.statement: A wet hymn-book page found in Saltmere Mine describes the sea giving back what it takes and has "M. Brand" pencilled in its margin.

sources.quote: About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: Records the physical clue without confirming who wrote it.

sources.quote: About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: Records where the page was found.

properties.what_changed: Mira heard the bell the night she left. Teo now identifies the "M. Brand" inscription on a Saltmere hymn page as Mira's handwriting and believes she was there; the GM has not confirmed this identification.

sources.quote: That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: Advances Teo's goal with his identification while keeping it a player inference.

change.name: Is Maren involved with the cult or choir?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa suspects Maren is behind events and in the cult; Oren suspects she runs the choir. Neither theory is confirmed.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.
You can think that. Roll investigation if you want to search the rest.

changes.why: Records the players' suspicion only as an unresolved thread.

sources.quote: Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

changes.why: Links the speculative thread to the existing Maren without changing her properties.

properties.details_shown: Previously described as having sunk into the bay with its bell. At low water its roof protrudes from the bay, with the bell tower and two broken arches; seaweed hangs from the stones. At midnight pale shapes stand in rows on the submerged chapel floor like a congregation, then vanish when the bell stops.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Adds the chapel descriptions and the witnessed shapes without identifying them.

change.name: Fishermen's warning about the Kelp Mother

properties.statement: Fishermen say the Kelp Mother takes children who stand too close to the water and pulls them down by the ankles; her existence is unconfirmed.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

changes.why: Stores the rumor without creating a Kelp Mother NPC.

properties.what_is_open: Who or what rings the submerged chapel bell? It rang twelve times again at midnight; the humming was much louder than two nights earlier, and pale shapes stood in rows on the submerged chapel floor until it stopped.

sources.quote: And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Advances the existing bell mystery with directly witnessed events.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.

changes.why: Uses the GM's explicit story-clock ruling to advance it from 2/6 to 3/6.

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the docks, with a fire going and the smell of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

changes.why: Records the new named location and its shown details.

properties.played_as: Huge, red-bearded; laughs at his own jokes and wipes the same mug throughout the conversation. Calls the party brave or stupid and offers stew on the house.
properties.knows: Says he has known Maren for thirty years and that she lost a brother to the bay; calls her sharp-tongued and good-hearted.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.
Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Records the new voiced innkeeper and attributes his knowledge claims to him.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.
The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

properties.next_step: The party plans to have Sela row them out tomorrow at first light and dive to the chapel at low tide during the day.
